OSPS-AC-01.01.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and accepts only secure methods, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

OSPS-AC-02.01.justification: A new member gets read access, the organization's base permission (gh api orgs/btclib-org --jq .default_repository_permission). Every higher grant is assigned by hand. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-AC-03.01.justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main. Its one bypass actor holds it in pull_request mode, which never allows a direct push. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-03.02.justification: The main-integrity ruleset forbids deleting main and has no bypass actor. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-04.01.justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at the organization and the repository, and cannot approve pull requests. Every workflow also sets permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning

OSPS-AC-04.02.justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top, and a job adds a write scope only where it uses it. zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does

OSPS-BR-01.01.justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run. Event fields and inputs reach run: steps only through env:, and zizmor's template-injection audit in the required lint check refuses the unsafe form. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml

OSPS-BR-01.03.justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request and pull_request_review_comment triggers, which give a fork no secrets and a read-only token. The review job, which holds a secret, runs only when the head repository is this one. The mention job holds a secret on any pull request's issue comment, and there checks out the default branch. It answers only users with write access, and its tools exclude Bash, edits, writes and file reads. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml

OSPS-BR-01.04.justification: No workflow_dispatch takes an input. A release tag's name is checked against the package version before anything is built. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml

OSPS-BR-02.01.justification: Each release has a unique calendar version (YYYY.M.D), set by a v* tag. release.yml refuses a tag that disagrees with the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/releases

OSPS-BR-02.02.justification: Every release asset carries the version in its file name: the sdist and the wheel, and the CycloneDX SBOM and the attestation bundle where a release has them. The attestation binds the other assets to their digests. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/releases/latest

OSPS-BR-03.01.justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://bitcoin-core-rpc.readthedocs.io/.

OSPS-BR-03.02.justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS only. PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations, and each GitHub release from v2026.8.12 on a Sigstore bundle. https://pypi.org/project/bitcoin-core-rpc/

OSPS-BR-04.01.justification: The GitHub release body is RELEASE_NOTES.md's entry: what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included. CHANGELOG.md lists every change. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

OSPS-BR-05.01.justification: Python dependencies come from PyPI, and the required test check runs the suite with uv from the committed uv.lock with --locked. pre-commit installs its hooks at the revisions .pre-commit-config.yaml names. Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#uvlock

OSPS-BR-06.01.justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing. Each GitHub release from v2026.8.12 on carries a Sigstore build-provenance bundle that binds the other assets to their SHA-256 digests, and its tag is signed. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/releases/latest

OSPS-BR-07.01.justification: Secret scanning and push protection are on, so a push carrying a recognised credential is refused. The detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.secrets.baseline

OSPS-BR-07.02.justification: A secret is an environment secret only the owners reach, and any other store's entry is recorded in the spending repository's REPOSITORY.md. A secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected, and the list is reviewed yearly. btclib-org/.github's tests/secrets_test.py refuses an unrecorded entry. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2913-L2940

OSPS-DO-01.01.justification: The user documentation is README.md, docs/source/migrating.md and the API reference. https://bitcoin-core-rpc.readthedocs.io/

OSPS-DO-02.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says where a defect is filed, and the bug-report form asks for what a report needs. SECURITY.md sends a vulnerability to a private channel instead. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml

OSPS-DO-03.01.justification: SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command for the release assets, and RELEASING.md the check that rebuilds the sdist from its tag. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-03.02.justification: The verify command pins the signer: --repo names this repository, --signer-workflow the organization's reusable-build.yml and --source-ref the release tag. SECURITY.md names the signer of each earlier release. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-04.01.justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, a fix ships as a new release, and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-05.01.justification: SECURITY.md: only the latest release is supported, so a release stops receiving security updates when the next one is published. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-06.01.justification: The package has no runtime dependency: pyproject.toml declares dependencies = []. uv obtains the development dependencies from PyPI and pins them in uv.lock, and Dependabot tracks them weekly with a seven-day cooldown. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#dependabot-and-pre-commitci

OSPS-DO-07.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md gives the build: uv is the only prerequisite, uv sync builds the environment from uv.lock, and uv build produces the sdist and wheel. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-01.01.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's Roles names who holds access to sensitive resources: the maintainer, the only bypass actor, and the three owners, each an administrator of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-01.02.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's Roles names the maintainer, the owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-02.01.justification: Proposed changes and usage obstacles are discussed publicly in the repository's GitHub issues (with a question form) and pull requests; cross-repository questions go to btclib-org/.github's tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/issues

OSPS-GV-03.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: one subject per pull request, the local gates, the review and the landing. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-03.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what a contribution must meet: one subject, a Signed-off-by trailer on every commit, the gates CI runs, 100% coverage, and a review against REVIEWING.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-04.01.justification: A grant of write or admin, to any repository of the organization, is an issue in btclib-org/.github that states the reason, and an owner other than the one asking approves it there. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/GOVERNANCE.md#L44-L46

OSPS-LE-01.01.justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer, Dependabot's and pre-commit.ci's aside. Web commits are signed off automatically. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py

OSPS-LE-02.01.justification: The source code is under the MIT license, which the OSI approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-02.02.justification: The released wheels and sdist declare License-Expression: MIT, the same OSI-approved license as the source. https://pypi.org/project/bitcoin-core-rpc/

OSPS-LE-03.01.justification: The license text is the repository's root LICENSE file. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-03.02.justification: The LICENSE file ships inside every release asset: the sdist root and the wheel's .dist-info/licenses/. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-QA-01.01.justification: The repository is public on GitHub at a static URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc

OSPS-QA-01.02.justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author, committer, date and signature; linear history and no force-pushes on main keep that record from being rewritten. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/commits/main

OSPS-QA-02.01.justification: pyproject.toml declares the direct dependencies: none at run time, and the development tools in dependency groups. The committed uv.lock pins them. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-02.02.justification: Each release from v2026.9.24 on attaches a CycloneDX 1.6 SBOM generated from the built wheel and covered by the release attestation. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/releases/latest

OSPS-QA-03.01.justification: main requires the listed status checks, up to date with main. enforce_admins is off, so an admin merge without them is a manual bypass, which the control allows. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-QA-04.01.justification: The organization standard's section 2 (*Which repositories, and how far*) lists every repository of btclib-org and its tier, and the organization profile lists the published packages. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far

OSPS-QA-04.02.justification: Each release is built from this one repository, and the package has no runtime dependency. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-05.01.justification: No generated executable is committed. The only binary file is the Sphinx inventory python.inv.

OSPS-QA-05.02.justification: No executable, library or compiled file is committed. The only binary files are an empty py.typed marker and docs/source/_inventories/python.inv, neither of them code.

OSPS-QA-06.01.justification: test.yml's aggregate check ('test: every job passed') runs the test suite on every pull request and is a required status check on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

OSPS-QA-06.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the suite and which workflows run it on every pull request, on main and on a schedule, and which of them gate a merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-QA-06.03.justification: The policy is 100% line and branch coverage (CONTRIBUTING.md, standard section 8). pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100, so untested new code fails the required test check. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-07.01.justification: main's ruleset requires one approving review, but the maintainer's pull_request-mode bypass remains, and recent pull requests landed without a non-author approval. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#review

OSPS-SA-01.01.justification: ARCHITECTURE.md gives the components and their layering. ASSURANCE_CASE.md's Threat model and Trust boundaries name the actors and what each can do. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md

OSPS-SA-02.01.justification: The API reference is generated from the docstrings of every module, and the required docs check fails when a name of __all__ is missing from the built page. https://bitcoin-core-rpc.readthedocs.io/

OSPS-SA-03.01.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the security assessment: what is claimed, the threat model, the trust boundaries and how each common implementation weakness is countered; SECURITY.md's limitations section records the known residual risks. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-SA-03.02.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* names the assets, adversaries and what is not defended, and *Trust boundaries* maps the attack surface where untrusted input enters, each argument naming the file, test or workflow behind it. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-VM-01.01.justification: SECURITY.md gives the private reporting channels and states the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md#L19

OSPS-VM-02.01.justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org, which reaches the three organization owners. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-VM-03.01.justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (the Security tab's 'Report a vulnerability') and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/security/advisories/new

OSPS-VM-04.01.justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories on this repository, each naming the release that fixes it: GHSA-cg87-q4qx-qw8p names v2026.10.8. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/security/advisories

OSPS-VM-04.02.justification: Each release's CycloneDX SBOM lists in its vulnerabilities array every vulnerability judged not to affect it, with the reason, from the tree's .github/vex.toml. None is judged so today, so the tree has no such file. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L3120-L3135

OSPS-VM-05.01.justification: Every pull request runs actions/dependency-review-action, which fails on an added or changed dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2892-L2909

OSPS-VM-05.02.justification: release.yml runs uv audit over every dependency the wheel declares before any publish job. An advisory, or a service it cannot reach, stops the release. The only exemption is an id the release's own signed VEX states as not affecting it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L3149-L3160

OSPS-VM-05.03.justification: The Dependency review job runs on every pull request and is a required check on main (lint / Dependency review), so a pull request that violates the policy cannot merge without an admin bypass. Policy: https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/7bc0f27d387604b70df8e4cb03afe873f6a821bb/README.md#L2892-L2909

OSPS-VM-06.01.justification: The standard's section 5 sets the threshold at zero: ruff runs select = ALL, bandit's S rules included, and each finding is fixed or suppressed in place with a reason. zizmor holds workflows to the same. CodeQL alerts have no stated threshold. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#5-ruff

OSPS-VM-06.02.justification: The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request (ruff with the S rules, strict mypy, zizmor, detect-secrets) and blocks the merge on any finding not suppressed in place with a reason. CodeQL also runs on every pull request but is not a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml

access_continuity.justification: The organization has three owners, fametrano, giacomocaironi and pmazzocchi, each an administrator of this repository and a reviewer of its publishing environments. If one becomes unavailable, the other two can still close issues, merge changes and release. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity

accessibility_best_practices.justification: bitcoin-core-rpc is a library with no user interface, so accessibility best practices have nothing to apply to. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

assurance_case.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md states the threat model, the trust boundaries, the secure-design argument and the argument against common implementation weaknesses this criterion asks for. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

automated_integration_testing.justification: test.yml runs the suite on every pull request and push to main that changes code, and its aggregate check is required on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

build_non_recursive.justification: This tree builds no native binaries, so there is no recursive-build question to answer. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_preserve_debug.justification: No native build or installation step exists to strip or preserve debugging information. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

build_repeatable.justification: Every week sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds the latest release's sdist from its tag. It passes only if the rebuilt file matches the release's attested digest byte for byte. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml

build_reproducible.justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit and normalized by .github/scripts/normalize_sdist.py. sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds the latest release's sdist from its tag every week and verifies it against the release's build-provenance attestation. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/actions/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml

build_standard_variables.justification: The package is pure Python on the uv_build backend: no compiler or linker runs, so CC, CFLAGS and LDFLAGS have nothing to reach. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

bus_factor.justification: Almost every commit is the maintainer's, and outside contributors have landed only a few pull requests. Continuity rests on the three organization owners, each an administrator of this repository. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md

code_of_conduct.justification: btclib-org/.github's CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is this repository's code of conduct, through GitHub's organization-wide default; the community-profile API reports it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

code_review_standards.justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/REVIEWING.md

coding_standards.justification: pyproject.toml selects every ruff rule (select = ["ALL"]) with a documented ignore list, and runs mypy in strict mode. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

coding_standards_enforced.justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy run as required pre-commit hooks, and lint.yml runs the same .pre-commit-config.yaml in CI, so the style is enforced automatically rather than by review alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml

contribution_requirements.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md names the gates a change must pass (suite at 100% coverage, pre-commit, docs build), the sign-off and the review; the coding standard is pyproject.toml's ruff `select = ["ALL"]` and mypy `strict = true`. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

contributors_unassociated.justification: One contributor accounts for almost all commits and pull requests (see bus_factor); no second significant contributor exists yet.

copyright_per_file.justification: Every Python file opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers". https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/__init__.py

crypto_algorithm_agility.justification: The client implements no cryptography of its own. TLS, when the RPC endpoint is https, is Python's standard library. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

crypto_call.justification: The only cryptography is TLS for an https endpoint, and it is Python's ssl module; the client implements none. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/transport.py

crypto_certificate_verification.justification: The TLS context sets verify_mode = CERT_REQUIRED and check_hostname = True, so an https endpoint's certificate and host name are verified. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/transport.py

crypto_credential_agility.justification: No credential is in the code: the client reads the node's cookie file from cookie_path at each call, or takes user and password as arguments, never inside the url. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

crypto_floss.justification: The only cryptography is TLS through Python's ssl module and OpenSSL, both FLOSS. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/transport.py

crypto_keylength.justification: TLS uses ssl.SSLContext, which since Python 3.10 refuses keys under 112 bits of security, NIST's floor through 2030. The floor here is Python 3.11. https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.10.html#ssl

crypto_pfs.justification: TLS uses ssl.SSLContext, which disables cipher suites without forward secrecy since Python 3.10. The floor here is Python 3.11. https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.10.html#ssl

crypto_published.justification: The only cryptography is TLS 1.2 or later through Python's ssl module, a published and reviewed protocol. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/transport.py

crypto_random.justification: The client generates no key or nonce. Its one random value, the JSON-RPC request id, is not a security value, and it comes from secrets.token_hex.

crypto_tls12.justification: TLS uses ssl.SSLContext, whose minimum version is TLS 1.2 since Python 3.10. The floor here is Python 3.11. https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.10.html#ssl

crypto_used_network.justification: The client speaks https or http, as the url names. https verifies the server over TLS. http is for a node on loopback, how Core's RPC is normally reached, and SECURITY.md says to use https or a tunnel for any other node. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

crypto_verification_private.justification: The TLS handshake, which verifies the certificate, completes before any request is sent, Authorization header included. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/transport.py

crypto_weaknesses.justification: TLS uses ssl.SSLContext, which disables SHA-1 MAC cipher suites and requires TLS 1.2 since Python 3.10. The floor here is Python 3.11. https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.10.html#ssl

crypto_working.justification: The only cryptography is TLS through ssl.SSLContext, whose defaults offer no broken algorithm. https://docs.python.org/3/whatsnew/3.10.html#ssl

dco.justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a pull request with a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer. Dependabot's and pre-commit.ci's commits are exempt. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py

delivery_mitm.justification: Distribution channels (GitHub, PyPI) use HTTPS exclusively.

dependency_monitoring.justification: Dependabot version updates cover uv and github-actions, and Dependabot security updates are on. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml

discussion.justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.

documentation_achievements.justification: README.md carries and links the OpenSSF Best Practices badge, beside the Scorecard badge. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

documentation_architecture.justification: ARCHITECTURE.md gives the four modules and their one import direction, errors < chains < transport < client, which tests/census_test.py enforces; none imports outside the standard library. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md

documentation_current.justification: The required docs check builds the documentation with sphinx-build -n -W on every pull request, and the API reference is generated from the docstrings. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml

documentation_quick_start.justification: README.md's *Talking to a node* and *Calling* sections walk a new user from install to a first RPC call. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

documentation_roadmap.justification: ROADMAP.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, covers the period until 2027-09-30, is reviewed every September, and states what is intended and what is deliberately not; this tree's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md

documentation_security.justification: SECURITY.md's Limitations, not vulnerabilities states the known limits: Basic Auth is cleartext over http, credentials are not zeroized, the environment chooses the TLS trust store, a caller's own transport is trusted, the node's chain is not checked unless asked, and nothing is retried. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

dynamic_analysis.justification: An automated test suite with 100% statement and branch coverage runs before every release (release.yml needs the test job); mutation.yml also runs weekly. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml

dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions.justification: The suite runs under pytest, which keeps every assert and turns every warning into an error (`filterwarnings = ["error"]` in pyproject.toml); nothing runs with python -O.

dynamic_analysis_unsafe.justification: This tree ships pure Python, a memory-safe language; it produces no software written in a memory-unsafe language for a dynamic memory-safety tool to run against. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

external_dependencies.justification: Every dependency is declared in machine-readable form in pyproject.toml's [project.dependencies] and dependency-groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

floss_license.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

floss_license_osi.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

governance.justification: GOVERNANCE.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, documents the decision model, the maintainer's bypass and every role a contributor, reviewer or owner holds; this tree's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md

hardened_site.justification: https://btclib.org/bitcoin-core-rpc/ is served over HTTPS with Content-Security-Policy (frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Strict-Transport-Security.

hardening.justification: ruff's select = ["ALL"] includes the bandit S rules, so a hardening defect such as unsafe deserialization or shell injection fails the lint gate. CodeQL also runs on every pull request and every push to main. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

implement_secure_design.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's Secure design principles applies each principle to this client, and SECURITY.md states the limits that remain. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

input_validation.justification: The client refuses input it cannot send faithfully: a url carrying credentials, a parameter that is not a JSON value, and a number that is not finite. With verify_chain or assert_chain, it also refuses a node on another chain. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

installation_common.justification: The package is on PyPI, and README.md gives the install command, pip install bitcoin-core-rpc. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

installation_development_quick.justification: uv sync installs the whole development environment in one command, as CONTRIBUTING.md's The environment and the gates says. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

installation_standard_variables.justification: Installation is pip install, which follows the interpreter's own install locations; the project has no installer of its own. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

interfaces_current.justification: ruff's UP and FA rules flag deprecated constructs, and pytest turns every warning into an error. deps-latest and deps-oldest run the suite weekly at the newest and the floor versions. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

internationalization.justification: bitcoin-core-rpc generates no end-user text and sorts no human-readable strings; its output (RPC results, errors) is technical data. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/README.md

know_common_errors.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Common implementation weaknesses* section names the errors that matter for an HTTP client and how each is countered: https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

know_secure_design.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles* section applies the principles to this client, and an owner other than the maintainer reviewed it on 2026-09-30: https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/issues/585

license_per_file.justification: Every Python file states "Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying LICENSE file or https://opensource.org/license/mit". https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/src/bitcoin_core_rpc/__init__.py

maintenance_or_update.justification: Only the latest release is supported and nothing is backported (SECURITY.md). RELEASING.md runs griffe check against the previous tag, and RELEASE_NOTES.md lists what a user must act on to upgrade. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

regression_tests_added50.justification: The required 100% line and branch coverage gate fails a fix whose new code no test runs. A merged pull request that changes src/ changes tests/ too, unless it changes only comments, docstrings or file locations. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged

release_notes_vulns.justification: The release notes name each vulnerability the release fixes: v2026.10.8 names GHSA-cg87-q4qx-qw8p, and v2026.10.4 the security review's issues. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/releases/tag/v2026.10.8

repo_distributed.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.

repo_interim.justification: development is on the main branch of https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc

repo_public.justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.

repo_track.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.

report_process.justification: Bugs are reported in the GitHub issue tracker with a bug-report form: https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml ; CONTRIBUTING.md's *The issue tracker* says what belongs there.

report_tracker.justification: Each repository uses its own GitHub Issues tracker for individual issues, with issue forms under .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, and an organization-wide tracker in btclib-org/.github for cross-repository findings. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/issues

require_2FA.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member. https://github.com/btclib-org

roles_responsibilities.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's Roles names the maintainer, the owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

secure_2FA.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication and allows only secure methods: TOTP apps, security keys or passkeys, and GitHub Mobile, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

security_review.justification: pmazzocchi, an owner other than the maintainer, reviewed the project on 2026-09-30. The review pins its scope to a commit, checks each claim of ASSURANCE_CASE.md, states what it did not cover and files each finding as an issue. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/issues/585

signed_releases.justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing, and each GitHub release from v2026.8.12 on a Sigstore provenance bundle. SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/releases/latest

sites_password_security.justification: Project sites are GitHub, PyPI and Read the Docs; none of these repositories runs a site of its own that stores user passwords -- authentication is GitHub's and PyPI's, not this project's. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

small_tasks.justification: Small tasks for new contributors carry the label "good first issue", which CONTRIBUTING.md sets aside for a first contribution. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/issues?q=label%3A%22good+first+issue%22

static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities.justification: ruff's select = ["ALL"] includes the bandit-derived S rules, which look for common vulnerabilities, and CodeQL's Python analysis runs on every pull request and every push to main. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

static_analysis_often.justification: lint.yml and codeql.yml run on every pull request and every push to main. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/actions/workflows/lint.yml

test.justification: test.yml runs the suite, gated at 100% line and branch coverage, and integration-bitcoind.yml runs the client against live bitcoind nodes; both are required checks on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

test_branch_coverage80.justification: Branch coverage is measured (branch = true) and the 100% gate counts it. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

test_continuous_integration.justification: test.yml runs the suite on every pull request and push to main that changes code, and its aggregate check is required on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

test_policy_mandated.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires 100% coverage, and fail_under = 100.0 fails the CI gate on any new code without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

test_statement_coverage80.justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0, gated on every pull request by test.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

test_statement_coverage90.justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100.0, gated on every pull request by test.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

tests_documented_added.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the 100% coverage gate, so new functionality is not accepted without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

two_person_review.justification: main's ruleset requires one approving review, but the maintainer's pull_request-mode bypass remains, and recent pull requests landed without a non-author approval. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#review

updateable_reused_components.justification: At run time the package reuses only the standard library. Its development tools are pinned in uv.lock and updated weekly by Dependabot. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml

version_semver.justification: Calendar versioning, YYYY.M.D, with the day as the micro level; each release is tagged v<version>. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github#12-releasing

version_tags_signed.justification: Release tags are signed from v2026.8.12 on, and RELEASING.md reads each signature back. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/tags

vulnerabilities_critical_fixed.justification: No publicly known vulnerability is left unfixed: GHSA-cg87-q4qx-qw8p is fixed in v2026.10.8, and no Dependabot alert is open. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/security/advisories

vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days.justification: No publicly known vulnerability is left unpatched. The findings of the 2026-09-30 security review were closed within four days, and GHSA-cg87-q4qx-qw8p was fixed in v2026.10.8 the day it was found. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/security/advisories

vulnerability_report_credit.justification: SECURITY.md and the review's issue credit the 2026-09-30 security review to pmazzocchi. GHSA-cg87-q4qx-qw8p had no outside reporter: the maintainer filed it from an audit of the organization's trees. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/issues/585

vulnerability_report_response.justification: Every vulnerability report so far was answered and closed within four days of being filed: the 2026-09-30 security review's findings and GHSA-cg87-q4qx-qw8p. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/security/advisories

vulnerability_response_process.justification: SECURITY.md's Reporting a vulnerability gives the private channels (a GitHub security advisory, or security at btclib dot org), who can see a report, and how a CVE is requested. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/SECURITY.md

warnings.justification: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_fixed.justification: warnings are not tolerated: mypy strict with all relevant extra checks activated, see https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_strict.justification: ruff runs with `select = ["ALL"]` (every rule family) and mypy runs with `strict = true`; both are required, zero-finding pre-commit hooks enforced again in the lint workflow. https://github.com/btclib-org/bitcoin-core-rpc/blob/main/pyproject.toml
